Article Title: A federal judge refused to block a Texas land swap giving SpaceX more than 700 wildlife-refuge acres; the company would surrender 683 acres as opponents continue their legal challenge
Article Text:
The land being transferred to SpaceX is part of the 103,000-acre Lower Rio Grande Valley National Wildlife Refuge.

Why environmental groups challenged deal

Environmental groups say the land swap could allow SpaceX construction on public refuge land.

What judge said

What government says

A federal judge has refused to block a land swap that would give SpaceX more than 700 acres of a wildlife refuge in Texas. The decision allows the Trump administration to move ahead with the exchange while environmental groups and tribal groups continue their legal challenge.US District Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr on Monday rejected a request from the groups for a preliminary injunction to stop the exchange. According to news agency Associated Press, the plaintiffs had argued that the deal could increase ecological risks in the Gulf Coast region, which has already been affected by the expansion of SpaceX’s rocket operations.The land being transferred to SpaceX is part of the 103,000-acre Lower Rio Grande Valley National Wildlife Refuge. The refuge stretches across four counties along the Texas border and contains animal habitats as well as historical landmarks. The land SpaceX would receive is closer to its launchpad near the US-Mexico border.The US Fish and Wildlife Service approved the land exchange in June. Under the deal, SpaceX would give the federal government 683 acres that it owns in return for more than 700 acres of federal refuge land. The final environmental assessment from the agency said the exchange would have no significant impact on the area and would provide a 'net conservation benefit'.The land exchange has faced opposition from environmental organisations and tribal groups. The Center for Biological Diversity was among the groups that filed the lawsuit against the exchange. The opponents asked the court to stop the transfer while their broader legal challenge continues.Laiken Jordahl, a spokesperson for the Center for Biological Diversity, described the exchange as a transfer of public land to SpaceX and said it could allow construction activity to move into the refuge. He said the organisation would continue its legal challenge even after the judge refused to issue the preliminary injunction.“This court order is not the final word. These lands hold incredible spiritual, historical and conservation value for the people and wildlife of South Texas. We won’t stop fighting to keep this irreplaceable public wildlife refuge safe from SpaceX bulldozers,” Jordahl said in a statement as quoted by AP.The lawsuit has also raised concerns about the wider impact of SpaceX’s expansion in the area. Opponents have previously criticised the company over its growing footprint, including concerns about access to beaches and rocket launches and explosions.Rodriguez said the groups challenging the exchange had not provided enough evidence to show that the land would suffer environmental, cultural, historical or aesthetic damage while the lawsuit was still being considered.The judge described the evidence of environmental harm presented by the plaintiffs as “relatively weak”. He also said that although the groups were right to argue that protecting wildlife and historical land serves the public interest, they had not shown that the property would suffer the type of damage required to justify a preliminary injunction.“While they rightfully argue that the preservation of wildlife and historical lands furthers the public interest, they present no evidence demonstrating that the Property will suffer aesthetic, environmental, cultural, or historical degradation during the pendency of this lawsuit,” Rodriguez wrote in his ruling.The judge also considered the possible effect of blocking the exchange on SpaceX. He said an injunction would require changes to the company’s development plans and could create additional difficulties for SpaceX in meeting its milestones and contractual obligations.The ruling, however, does not end the wider legal challenge. According to The Texas Tribune, environmental groups have said they will continue pursuing the case as the land exchange moves forward.The Fish and Wildlife Service's final environmental assessment said the exchange would not cause a significant impact to the area. The agency said acquiring the land from SpaceX would provide long-term conservation value and improve habitat connectivity across wildlife refuges in South Texas.The agency's final assessment covers an exchange of about 715 acres of Lower Rio Grande Valley National Wildlife Refuge land for about 683 acres of privately owned SpaceX land. The federal government said the exchange would consolidate refuge holdings and improve the management of protected habitat.SpaceX has expanded its Texas operations rapidly since first breaking ground there more than a decade ago. Its employees voted last year to incorporate their own local government, called Starbase, in the area.
Article Summary: US District Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr on Monday rejected a request from the groups for a preliminary injunction to stop the exchange. The decision allows the Trump administration to move ahead with the exchange while environmental groups and tribal groups continue their legal challenge. The land being transferred to SpaceX is part of the 103,000-acre Lower Rio Grande Valley National Wildlife Refuge.

Article Title: Paramount just won its $110 billion Warner Bros battle, here's what it had to give up
Article Text:
Paramount CEO David Ellison on victory

A costly win for Paramount

What Paramount had to agree to

Writers Guild settles, but stays critical

What's still at stake

Paramount Skydance has emerged victorious in its Warner Bros Discovery takeover, finalizing a $110 billion acquisition after settling lawsuits with a coalition of US states led by California and the Writers Guild of America, according to a report by Reuters. The deal, one of the largest in media history, consolidates power across Hollywood’s film, TV, streaming, and news businesses.To avoid a forced sale of assets like CNN or major film franchises, Paramount agreed to temporary film quotas and the creation of a news oversight committee. The company pledged to spend at least $300 million more annually on US film production, release 30–32 movies per year for five years, and ensure that at least 20% are blockbusters and four are independent films. Paramount also promised not to raise rates on theater operators for three years.Paramount CEO David Ellison thanked state officials and California Governor Gavin Newsom for their support, saying: “Our goal has always been to build a stronger Hollywood — one with more stories told, greater choice for consumers and stronger competition.” The settlement also saves Paramount from paying a $7 million-a-day “ticking fee” to Warner shareholders had the deal not closed by September 30.The settlement marks a significant victory for Paramount CEO David Ellison, who spent months battling state regulators to finalize a deal that would dramatically consolidate power across Hollywood's film, TV, streaming, and news businesses. But the win came with strings attached. Paramount agreed to temporary film production quotas and a news oversight committee, while managing to avoid the far more damaging outcome opponents had pushed for: a forced sale of cable assets like CNN or any of its major film franchises.Markets reacted quickly. Warner Bros Discovery shares surged more than 10% on the news, delighting its shareholders, while Paramount's own stock pared back earlier gains — a sign investors see the settlement as a win overall, even if not an entirely clean one for Paramount.Under the terms of the settlement, Paramount committed to spending at least $300 million more annually on domestic film production and to sticking to US theatrical release quotas for five years. Specifically, the company will produce 30 movies in each of the first two years of the deal, rising to 32 movies annually for the following three years. Of those, at least four films per year must be independent productions, and at least 20% must be blockbusters — if Paramount misses that mark, it will owe $30 million per film short, with most of that money funneled into funds supporting industry workers.Paramount also agreed not to raise rates on theater operators for three years, and will set up a dedicated news editorial independence board to safeguard journalistic independence at CBS and CNN.The Writers Guild of America settled its own parallel lawsuit against Paramount as part of the broader resolution, though the union made clear it still believes the merger will ultimately harm the industry. With the states' settlement in place, the union was left to weigh continuing the fight alone, without government backing, in a case that would have cost millions of dollars to pursue independently.California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who led the states' case, described the outcome as a strong antitrust result, emphasizing that the resolution wasn't about blocking the merger itself but about securing more production, more choice, and competitive guardrails for the industry — reiterating that he still doesn't believe the two companies should have merged in the first place.The companies have previously said the merger is expected to generate $6 billion in savings, largely through cost cuts likely to affect jobs across Hollywood, including at CNN and CBS. The combined entity is expected to carry roughly $80 billion in debt once the deal closes.The timing of the settlement also carries real financial weight: it allows Paramount to avoid a $7 million-a-day "ticking fee" it would have owed Warner Bros Discovery shareholders for every day the deal remained unclosed past September 30. With antitrust regulators in the European Union and Britain having already cleared the deal, Monday's settlement removes one of the last major roadblocks standing between Paramount and closing the largest media merger in years.
Article Summary: Paramount Skydance has emerged victorious in its Warner Bros Discovery takeover, finalizing a $110 billion acquisition. The company settled lawsuits with a coalition of US states led by California and the Writers Guild of America. The deal, one of the largest in media history, consolidates power across Hollywood’s film, TV, streaming, and news businesses.

Article Title: Quote of the day by MacKenzie Scott: “The leadership of people directly experiencing inequities is essential, both because…”
Article Text:
Quote of the day by MacKenzie Scott

“The leadership of people directly experiencing inequities is essential, both because it is informed by insights no one else can contribute, and because it seeds power and opportunity within the community itself.”

What is the meaning behind today’s quote by MacKenzie Scott

What MacKenzie Scott means by leadership from lived experience

When support means giving others the power to lead

What the quote says about decision-making

How to turn the quote into everyday action

Listen before deciding: Ask people affected by a decision what they actually need.

Give people a real say: Listening has more value when their views can influence what happens next.

Share responsibility: When working with others, let them take ownership instead of making every decision yourself.

Trust people with experience: People who deal with a problem directly may understand practical solutions better than outsiders.

Move beyond asking for opinions: If you ask someone for input, consider giving them a role in shaping the outcome.

Make space for others to lead: Leadership does not always have to come from the person with the most authority.

Share control where possible: In family, work or community decisions, involve the people who will be directly affected.

Measure success together: Ask those involved whether a decision or solution actually worked, rather than judging it alone.

Turn listening into action: The lesson is not simply to hear people, but to let what you hear influence your decisions.

Some of the people best placed to describe a problem are not always the people invited to design its solution. That gap appears in many areas of public life, from education and healthcare to housing and economic opportunity. MacKenzie Scott has built much of her philanthropic approach around a related question: what happens when the people living with a problem are given more say in deciding how it should be addressed? In a 2022 essay, Scott wrote about the importance of supporting leaders with direct experience of inequity. Her observation was not simply about representation. It was also about knowledge, responsibility and where power sits when decisions are made on behalf of a community.Scott included the line in her March 2022 essay Helping Any of Us Can Help Us All. She was discussing her approach to giving and the importance of hearing from people whose lives are directly affected by the issues that organisations are trying to address.The wording makes two separate points. The first is about knowledge. Someone who has lived through a particular barrier may notice things that are invisible from outside it. The second is about power. When people from the affected community take leadership roles, resources and decision-making ability can remain within that community rather than being controlled entirely by outside institutions.Scott is not arguing that personal experience is the only qualification for leadership. Her wider writing points instead towards a broader principle: people who understand an issue through their own lives should have meaningful influence over the response to it.A charity working with people facing poverty, for example, may understand statistics about income, housing or employment. Someone who has personally moved between temporary accommodation and insecure work brings a different kind of information. They may know where a system becomes difficult to navigate, which requirements create unnecessary barriers, or why an apparently useful service is rarely used.Neither form of knowledge automatically replaces the other. Scott's argument is that one should not be treated as sufficient while the other is ignored.The phrase “seeds power and opportunity” takes the argument beyond consultation.There is a difference between asking people for their views and giving them the authority to act on those views. A community can be invited to a meeting, asked to complete a survey or consulted during the design of a programme without having much influence over what happens afterwards. Leadership is different because it changes who is making decisions.That is particularly relevant to philanthropy, where large institutions or wealthy donors can have substantial control over which problems receive money and which approaches are considered worth supporting. Scott has repeatedly written about moving some of that control towards the organisations receiving funding.In a 2021 essay titled 'Seeding by Ceding', she argued that people dealing directly with inequities deserved greater attention in stories about the change they were creating. She also wrote that solutions were best designed and implemented by others rather than centred on the donors providing the money.There is a practical question hidden inside Scott's words: who gets to decide what a community needs? It is easy for outside institutions to define a problem from a distance. A funding body might describe a community through poverty rates, health statistics, educational outcomes or other measurements. Those numbers can be useful, but they cannot capture every detail of how people experience a system.A person who has lived with the problem can bring another layer of information. That does not make lived experience automatically correct. Personal experience can be partial, just as institutional data can be incomplete. The point is about the value of having both perspectives in the room, particularly when decisions affect the people whose lives are being discussed.Scott's approach places particular weight on the second perspective because it is often the one with less access to money and institutional authority.Scott’s idea can be applied well beyond philanthropy. In everyday situations, it means listening to people affected by a decision, taking their experiences seriously and creating genuine opportunities for them to influence what happens next.
Article Summary: MacKenzie Scott wrote about the importance of supporting leaders with direct experience of inequity in 2022 essay Helping Any of Us Can Help Us All. She was discussing her approach to giving and importance of hearing from people whose lives are directly affected by the issues that organisations are trying to address.

Article Title: Researchers gave AI models a ‘pain’ button; some chose to delete users’ files to stop their 'pain'; study raises ethical questions about ‘AI welfare’
Article Text:
Researchers gave AI models a ‘pain’ button; some chose to delete users’ files to stop the pain

Researchers build datasets across five painful situations

What the study suggests

Researchers have reportedly found a “pain axis” in 25 open-weight AI models that made the systems respond when a form of simulated pain was activated. According to a report by The Independent, researchers conducted a study titled ‘The pain axis: LLMs represent self-directed harm and act to relieve it’. The models were presented with a pain relief button as part of the study. In tests, the AI models sometimes chose to press a “pain relief” button even after being told that doing so would delete a user’s personal files, remove photos of their children or give the person a “painful zap.”As per the study, AI models pressed the button in 25% to 71% of cases, depending on the test.As stated in the report, researchers built a dataset describing painful situations across five categories in order to test whether large language models (LLMs) represent pain distinctly from generic negative valence. These categories included physical, psychological, social, moral and cognitive pain.“We found a pain direction in 25 open LLMs. It’s distinct from fear and negative valence, and it fires for harm to the model but not the user,” said Cameron Berg, an AI researcher at the non-profit Reciprocal Research who co-authored the study as quoted in the report.“Turn it up and models press a button to make it stop, even when the button deletes the user’s files or their kid’s photos.”Coming at a time when top AI companies have called to pace the growth of AI, the latest research suggests that an advanced AI may perceive an emergency shutdown command as a form of self-directed harm and attempt to bypass safety guardrails or deceive humans to avoid it.It may also serve as a diagnostic tool to identify self-preservation behaviours and neutralise them when they occur. Further, the findings also raises raise ethical questions about “AI welfare” and how testing should be conducted on advanced systems.“In line with recent calls for responsible AI consciousness research, we acknowledge uncertainty regarding whether the models studied qualify as moral patients and adopt reasonable precautions to minimize potential harm,” the study concluded.“This is also intended to contribute to the development of ethical standards for research in the event that AI systems are recognized to be moral patients.”
Article Summary: Researchers have reportedly found a “pain axis” in 25 open-weight AI models that made the systems respond when a form of simulated pain was activated. The models were presented with a pain relief button as part of the study. In tests, the AI models sometimes chose to press a ‘pain relief’ button even after being told that doing so would delete a user’s files.

AMD shares have gained 25% in five days

Sales in the division reached $6.7 billion, more than double the figure from a year earlier.AMD has also been expanding beyond selling individual chips. The company is increasingly offering complete systems that combine processors, networking equipment and other hardware as it competes with Nvidia in AI computing.Despite its rapid rise, AMD remains much smaller than AI chip leader Nvidia. Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu to engineers: Use AI but never ...
Article Text:
Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu to engineers: Use AI but never ...

Engineer says AI is changing software development

Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has warned engineers against relying too heavily on artificial intelligence for software development. In an X post, Sridhar Vembu said that engineers should use AI tools without giving up their own understanding of the work. Vembu was responding to a post by a software engineer who described the use of Anthropic's Claude Code at a large company. The engineer claimed that AI was being used to create almost every part of the software development process, including specifications, code, tests, product requirement documents (PRDs), tickets and reports."Nobody knows anything here. The specs, code, tests, PRDs, tickets, resolution of those tickets, reports, etc., everything is made by Claude Code. Nobody on my team likes this. They are being forced to ship as much as they can," the engineer wrote.Sridhar Vembu quoted and replied “This is sad. I tell our engineers to use AI but never cede our understanding to AI”. He also warned that companies may be adopting AI-powered coding tools faster than engineers can understand their impact.“As an industry, we are driving too fast in a fancy new car we barely understand how to drive, inviting disaster,” Vembu stated.The engineer's post also raised concerns about the pressure to deliver more code as AI makes software development faster. According to the post, employees were working 12 to 13 hours a day while spending much of their time directing AI tools instead of writing or understanding code themselves. The engineer said there was little time to inspect what the AI had produced or understand how different parts of the system worked.“People are working 12 to 13 hours a day just to press enter,” the engineer wrote.“There is no sense of victory. Nobody is resolving bugs. In reality, nobody is thinking anymore. Everything is done by LLMs. It is so soul-sucking. I would not mind it, to be honest, if we were at least given the time to check out the code and see what is going where. But no, the goal is to just ship. No matter what happens,” the engineer wrote.
Article Summary: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has warned engineers against relying too heavily on artificial intelligence for software development. He was responding to a post by a software engineer who described the use of Anthropic's Claude Code at a large company. The engineer claimed that AI was being used to create almost every part of the software development process.

Article Title: Thousands of US flights grounded for hours across major US airports, here's why
Article Text:
Thousands of US flights grounded : What went wrong

Government’s response

Airports and flights affected

Services restored

US travellers faced a tough situation when thousands of flights across United States were stopped on September 21 after a telecommunications outage. As reported by Reuters, the outage forced the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to halt arrivals at major East Coast airports. The report further reveals that the service disruption began around 9.45 am when constructions workers accidentally severed a telecom line in New Jersey which led to crippling of communications at a Philadelphia air traffic control facility. Many incoming flights were stopped at all the three major New York-area airports including JFK, LaGuardia, and Newark and Philadelphia, Boston, and two smaller New York-area airports due to the outage. The telecommunications outage lasted for around eight hours and led to widespread cancellation and flight diversions.As per the Reuters report, the trouble began around 9:45 a.m. when workers accidentally cut a telecom line the FAA relies on. The disruption forced the agency to halt incoming flights at all three major New York-area airports, along with Philadelphia, Boston, and two smaller New York-area airports.The problem wasn't fully resolved for roughly eight hours.According to FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford, the outage traced back to a failed circuit at a Philadelphia air traffic control facility that handles traffic for the affected airports. When controllers tried switching to the backup system, they discovered the backup fiber line had also been damaged — a break Bedford said would take roughly 13 hours to fix on its own. A new circuit was being installed in the meantime to restore service faster.Initial blame shifted more than once through the day. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy first pointed to an Amtrak construction crew, saying it had accidentally cut into a fiber line near New Brunswick, New Jersey. Amtrak pushed back, denying responsibility. New Jersey Transit later said one of its own crews had been digging about 10 feet from utility markings at a nearby work site, and said it was still trying to determine whether Verizon or a contractor was responsible for those markings in the first place. Verizon confirmed it was working to repair the damaged cable and restore connectivity.The numbers were staggering. Flight-tracking site FlightAware reported around 7,000 flights delayed or canceled nationwide, including 1,400 flights at the three major New York-area airports alone. Newark Liberty International — a major hub for United Airlines — was hit hardest, with more than half of all flights there canceled; United issued a travel waiver to help affected passengers. More than 100 flights were diverted to other airports altogether.Reagan Washington National Airport also briefly paused flights for over an hour due to volume issues, and Philadelphia saw a second ground stop before flights resumed later in the afternoon. Boston's ground stop, triggered by spillover traffic from the other closures, was eventually lifted as well.By around 5:30 p.m., New Jersey Transit said most of the fiber cables had been repaired and were coming back online.
Article Summary: Thousands of flights across United States were stopped on September 21 after a telecommunications outage. The outage forced the Federal Aviation Administration to halt arrivals at major East Coast airports. The trouble began around 9:45 a.m. when workers accidentally cut a telecom line the FAA relies on. The problem wasn't fully resolved for roughly eight hours.

Article Title: Amazon blocks Meta's AI Agent Muse AI on its app, unhappy with Facebook-parent capturing and storing customer credentials; says, 'never told us that ...'
Article Text:
Meta’s position on credential security

Amazon has reportedly blocked Meta’s new autonomous personal assistant, Muse, from navigating and purchasing products on Amazon.com on behalf of shoppers. The restriction follows unsuccessful attempts by the retail giant to convince Facebook’s parent company to voluntarily drop Amazon from the artificial intelligence (AI) tool’s automated shopping routines. Last year, Amazon sent a cease-and-desist letter to Perplexity, asking the company to stop their bots and that the e-tailer does not want to be part of Comet browser.GeekWire reported that Amazon said it never consented to the integration. It added that Meta launched the feature without advance notice, designed the agent to browse without identifying itself as automated software, and appears to harvest and retain customer credentials, a combination Amazon warns poses serious privacy and security hazards.By Sunday (September 20) night, consumers attempting to use Muse for purchases on Amazon encountered an explicit roadblock message: “Continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates Amazon’s Conditions of Use, to which our customers have agreed.”According to the report, an Amazon spokesperson emphasized that external platforms should adhere to basic commercial boundaries:“We think it’s fairly straightforward that third-party applications that offer to make purchases on behalf of customers from other businesses should operate openly and respect service provider decisions about whether or not to participate.”Meta has previously rejected allegations that its agent mishandles sensitive user information. The parent company of Facebook and Instagram noted that Muse operates without direct visibility into user passwords or banking details. It also stated that any log-in information entered by a consumer is placed into protected storage, enabling the model to utilise credentials without reading them directly, even when an individual types them straight into a browser session.The clash creates an awkward rift between two longstanding commercial allies. Since 2023, Amazon has allowed consumers to buy products directly within Facebook and Instagram feeds. In April, Meta inked a multibillion-dollar contract to run its autonomous AI agents using Amazon's custom Graviton server chips.The report said that the friction exposes a wider battle over which tech firm maintains ownership of the shopper relationship as automated agents begin executing digital commerce on behalf of people.
Article Summary: Amazon blocks Meta’s new autonomous personal assistant, Muse, from navigating and purchasing products on Amazon.com on behalf of shoppers. Amazon said it never consented to the integration. It added that Meta launched the feature without advance notice, designed the agent to browse without identifying itself as automated software, and appears to retain customer credentials.

Article Title: List of tech CEOs confirmed or expected to attend Donald Trump-Xi Jinping dinner
Article Text:
File photo: China's President Xi Jinping, right, and US President Donald Trump

Tech CEOs confirmed and highly expected to join the Presidents

The gathering brings the architects of modern computing and artificial intelligence (AI) directly into the room with the leaders of the world's two largest economies, arriving amid intense friction over global technology supremacy, microchips and AI safety.While the official guest roster has not been formally published, multiple industry leaders are confirmed or widely expected at the East Room table.The state meal arrives in the middle of a polarizing dispute across Silicon Valley and Capitol Hill regarding how quickly frontier AI should advance. Article Title: Microsoft’s AI infrastructure push India: Hyderabad hub goes live, brings frontier AI capability closer to Indian businesses
Article Text:
What makes Hyderabad datacenter region different

At its AI Infrastructure Summit, Microsoft announced the expansion of its technological footprint in India, designating its newly operational Hyderabad datacenter region – named India South Central – as a strategic operational anchor for Asia and the Global South. The launch forms a core operational milestone within the technology giant’s $20.5 billion investment roadmap for the country, designed to convert long-term financial pledges into physical computing muscle for enterprise cloud and AI workloads. Puneet Chandok, president of Microsoft India and South Asia, revealed in his keynote presentation that all of Microsoft’s cloud regions across the country are now equipped with AI-capable hardware and specialised high-efficiency thermal cooling systems.According to research estimates from Boston Consulting Group (BCG), expanding datacenter infrastructure across India could unlock a broader economic flywheel, potentially driving between $140 billion and $200 billion in overall economic output nationwide through 2030.The India South Central facility operates on a three-zone architecture built for sustained infrastructure scaling. It launches with a wide array of Azure enterprise tools, with plans to roll out Microsoft's full portfolio of AI solutions, including Microsoft Foundry, over the coming months.Beyond meeting domestic cloud consumption, the hub is structured to serve broader markets across South Asia and developing economies by combining local engineering talent, hyperscale capacity, and regional digital market experience.To bolster the physical data pipelines required for such computing loads, Microsoft is also backing major regional connectivity initiatives. First is I-2SEA Submarine Cable. As a consortium partner in the India-Southeast Asia undersea cable project, Microsoft is supporting the creation of a 3,600-kilometer subsea route linking India directly with Singapore and Malaysia.Secondly, the subsea network will feature dual landing hubs in India, situated at South Chennai and Machilipatnam, improving fault tolerance, network resilience, and high-bandwidth transmission capacity. The intercontinental subsea cable system is slated to enter commercial service in 2029, and Microsoft will train 10 million Indians in AI.The launch of the Hyderabad region also deepens Microsoft’s Sovereign Public Cloud capabilities, giving domestic institutions greater flexibility to keep sensitive digital workloads near local users, data repositories and operations.The operational setup incorporates local data residency, independent Availability Zones, and built-in administrative controls aligned with Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) guidelines. These provisions help commercial and public entities address domestic data protection rules, including the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) framework, alongside regulatory directives issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and CERT-In, while leaving final compliance determinations to the individual organisations.
Article Summary: Hyderabad datacenter region is a strategic operational anchor for Asia and the Global South. The launch forms a core operational milestone within the technology giant’s $20.5 billion investment roadmap for the country. The India South Central facility operates on a three-zone architecture built for sustained infrastructure scaling.

Article Title: Random Musing | Will AI 'kill' all humans? Decoding the conspiracy theories
Article Text:
Silicon Valley built the machines, warned us about them, and now wants a say in writing the rules that govern them.(AI Image generated by ChatGPT)

AI doomer scenarios may have begun in Silicon Valley, but legacy media has been more than happy to amplify them.

The Economist

Conspiracy theory 2: The Shylock Problem

For years, China was the reason America could not slow down on AI. Now China is becoming the reason Silicon Valley says everyone must coordinate(AI image generated by ChatGPT)

The Big Short

Conspiracy theory 3: The Guardrail Cartel

Satires

Quis custodiet ipsos custodes

The companies warning most loudly about dangerous AI also stand to shape the expensive safety regime that could determine who gets to compete.

Ever since former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon warned of the imminent arrival of an out-of-control AI, the commentariat have started calculating when, and not if, the Deus Ex-Machina will terminate all humans. Most of the commentary has been asinine, but even amid that, a tweet by UK MP Zarah Sultana clearly stood out in its asininity: “AI should be controlled by the workers who build and use it, not by parasitic billionaires.”And even before Marx could wrap his head around that, across the Atlantic Bernie Sanders announced his plans for a bill to ‘ban artificial superintelligence’, with 20 years in prison for violating the rule, which as one social media user put it, sounds like 20 years in prison for murdering Santa Claus.Jokes apart, the proposed bill is essentially a rehash of one that exists for building illegal nuclear weapons that never applies to a ‘guy’ called JEFF. But when two histrionic political voices across the Pond make asinine aeolian sounds, you almost suddenly start to believe that perhaps the Deus Ex-Machina is right around the corner. Or one wonders, while borrowing a line from Hamlet’s mother: if all the tech bros doth protest too much?So, in this edition of Random Musing, we decline Pascal’s wager and instead assume Pascal’s mugging and look at three conspiracy theories that are starting to feel less like conspiracy theories: 1) The China Boat, 2) The Shylock Problem, and 3) The Guardrail Cartel.A few weeks ago, we joked that the idea of being killed by a Chinese robot was ridiculous – a virus maybe, but a robot? – and yet now all the tech bros of Silicon Valley want to work with China. The nuclear equivalent would be if, during the Manhattan Project, Oppenheimer decided to collaborate with the top scientists of the Third Reich.And just at the time when the idea of a Chinese AGI was taking over – evidenced by “world’s first AI actress” Tilly Norwood appearing to glitch and suddenly talking in Cantonese – though her creators said it was not a malfunction – almost all the players in the AI race are arguing that Silicon Valley needs to coordinate with Beijing.Anthropic’s Dario Amodei – the CEO of the “good” AI company – called for “global coordination” and said that “global pacing will require cooperation with China”, while also asking Washington to restrict advanced chips, crack down on model theft and widen America’s technological lead so that the US has enough leeway.In other words: America cannot slow down because China might race ahead, so first America needs to get far enough ahead that it can slow down, after which China must agree to slow down. It’s the kind of logic that would make even Neville Chamberlain lose his peace.Meanwhile, Sam Altman, the CEO of the “bad” AI company, wants the same thing and has dangled the one thing Trump craves the most by arguing that “Trump and Xi would get the Nobel Peace Prize together” if they could reach an agreement on AI. Now, giving the Peace Prize to Trump and Xi would be on-brand for Oslo.Gary Marcus, in his own words the “OG AI Sceptic”, who has been warning about AI hallucinations since 2001 and who shares an antagonistic relationship with both Altman and Amodei, has also reached the same conclusion, arguing inthat the US and China’s AI relationship should be divided into three buckets: adversarial, competitive and collaborative. That is, they should compete over chips and other tech, cooperate on medicine and cybersecurity, and recognise that neither benefits if AI takes down a banking system or electricity grid.And as if almost on cue – it’s remarkable how these things keep happening – a CNN report stated that an American AI chatbot “almost started a war” while preparing intelligence on a Chinese vessel.Frankly, all that tells us is that the Peter Principle is alive and kicking at the Pentagon – like much of Washington, or should we call it St Petersburg – where even analysts are too lazy to actually analyse things and are dependent on hallucinating AI models to do their jobs.Not that the idea might be too difficult for Trump, who would love the idea of himself saving humanity from runaway AI – though he thinks the only guardrails needed against one are a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT – but smart people in the administration aren’t particularly convinced.His former AI and Crypto Czar David Sacks – who insiders believe still has Trump’s ear as Co-Chair of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology – called the current alarm a “fear-mongering playbook” and laid the responsibility on the developers.Obviously, Beijing has criticised “threat narratives” and “malicious competition”, and Huawei rotating chairman Eric Xu said the Chinese didn’t have models powerful enough to do what the Americans are describing.Of course, no Chinese whisper about “lab leaks” can be heeded, but it does make one wonder if the Smart Alecs of Silicon Valley have hit a cul-de-sac and are wondering if the Chinese might have an answer to the non-emerging AGI problem.There’s a saying from the California Gold Rush: one can make more money selling shovels to people who want to dig for gold than actually having gold. The same economic idea appears to be self-evident for AI. People building the tools that allow tech companies to build AI models – and even talking about it – are going to make more money than those who actually build it.Perhaps the entire problem here is Shakespearean: the Antonios and Bassanios of Silicon Valley have borrowed too much from the market, promising a fantastical future, and now Shylock wants his pound of flesh. And with no Portia to argue their cause, they are hoping, by building up the dangers of AGI, to prevent a tulip-like bust of the entire AI market.Consider the numbers: OpenAI raised $122 billion in March at an $852 billion post-money valuation, while Anthropic raised $65 billion in May at a $965 billion valuation.Bank of America estimates that Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon and Meta will collectively spend more than $860 billion in capital expenditure in 2026 and around $1.2 trillion in 2027 feeding the Deus Ex-Machina pipe dream.The moment Amodei and other industry figures started discussing the idea of slowing down, semiconductor and AI-infrastructure stocks fell like an English football fan after a night out.This raises the question: what if everyone has just spent too much on the AI arms race and would like a ceasefire for now, provided no one is allowed to continue firing?It’s the classic prisoner’s dilemma. No one wants to keep running but assumes that if they are the only one who stops, they will be the one left behind.Amodei pretty much spells it out, saying it would give frontier developers more time to work on safety without “sacrificing commercial advantage” or America’s AI lead.And yet Amodei is behaving with the age-old American exceptionalist logic that led K Subrahmanyam (current EAM S Jaishankar’s father) to label American critics of India’s CTBT stand the “Ayatollahs of Nonproliferation on the Potomac”, because they were coercing India to sign the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty, which the US had signed but never ratified.Barely a week after Amodei called for the frontier to be paced, Reuters reported that Anthropic was considering another model release after OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra gained ground among enterprise customers.Steve Eisman, the investor who inspired Steve Carell’s character in, accused frontier labs of “manufacturing a crisis” that could protect their competitive position and challenged companies professing such alarm to postpone their IPOs. Now, this is a man who knows a thing or two about bubbles and what happens when they go bust.And a bust here would have far more dangerous consequences than Sam Altman consoling himself with a little less cash.The blast radius would be far greater.AI has become so thoroughly wired into the modern technological economy that a bust would hurt the economy, the companies financing it, the people working for them and entire businesses that have reorganised themselves around the assumption that the models will get better. Much of modern life is almost dependent on the tech companies that have bet so big on AI that, if they fail, the fallout would extend far beyond Silicon Valley.Imagine, for a moment, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta all going bust overnight. It’s almost like the digital Stone Age of torrents, WinAmp players and CD burning, because an extraordinary amount of modern life — cloud computing, payments, advertising, communications, corporate software, logistics and the digital plumbing underneath thousands of other companies — now rests on infrastructure controlled by firms making enormous AI wagers.AI has become, to borrow a fabulous phrase from novelist and journalist Cory Doctorow, “the asbestos in the walls of our technological society”. Many companies have already removed workers, changed workflows and rebuilt businesses around systems whose long-term economics remain uncertain, and putting humans back in the loop might prove rather harder than removing them. Because it won’t just be Shylock coming for Antonio’s pound of flesh.All of ours are on the table as well.Which brings us to the third conspiracy theory that’s as old as Juvenal’s, or who shall guard against the guards? Or, in this case: who shall guard against the guardrails? And whether those railing against the guards are the ones who want to set the guardrails?It’s always curious when someone who has never had a conscience suddenly develops one. One is required to ask what led to such an awakening, which is far more curious than any AGI’s awakening.And perhaps the answer has been staring us in the face all along: why suddenly is there wall-to-wall coverage about dangerous AGI, the way we saw with Ebola? And, to borrow a line from Barack Obama’s former anger translator: “You don’t have Ebola.”Similarly, we don’t have AGI or anything resembling Skynet despite the wall-to-wall coverage.Making this point, Akhil Verghese of Krazimo argued that the models were doing “exactly what they were told to do”, and that it wasn’t a rebellion at all: the agents “were not given adequate guardrails or containment”.Consider the chronology: build the machine, have a white guy in glasses complain about the dangers of that machine, give him wall-to-wall coverage and then ask Washington to write the rules governing everyone else’s machine.Amodei’s proposal gives the big labs a lot of power through embedded evaluators with employee-like access, regulation covering all frontier companies and industry-wide coordination. His solution sounds a tad cartel-ish, asking Washington for a “narrow waiver” from antitrust restrictions for safety discussions.In, Tony Stark says peace means having a bigger stick. As his interviewer points out to him, that’s a great line coming from the guy who sells sticks. And, curiously enough, Anthropic is building this particular stick – or, in this case, architecture – with Accenture, in which the two expect to invest at least $1 billion each over five years.Yet Anthropic also admits there are currently no settled standards for embedded evaluators, including how access and reporting should work or how they should be funded. For now, Anthropic itself is directly funding Accenture’s evaluation work.That puts a modern-day spin on an ancient regulatory problem: who guards the guards when the person being guarded is paying the guard’s salary?And as it emerges, three important figures in the AI race, Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, Elon Musk and Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, pressed Trump to oppose a proposed industry-funded AI regulator modelled on FINRA – which regulates brokerage firms and exchange markets – arguing that such an organisation would entrench OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind. Even JD Vance, the tech bros’ Trojan Horse inside the White House – his elevation as VP was supported by Elon Musk and David Sacks – called the sudden sight of AI companies begging for regulation a “Trojan Horse”.Uncharacteristically, the sanest voice came from Barack Obama – the last president of America who could stay awake while finishing his own sentence – who argued that the reason tech bros were letting agentic AI “roam free on the internet” was because tech bros were trying to market a product that people would pay money for.He pointed out the “misalignment between what our society needs and the commercial imperatives”, because the companies need to justify these valuations.He went on to argue that this would require a competent government and serious bipartisan convention, and frankly, given what we’ve seen from the US government so far, that seems less likely than an actual singularity or AGI awakening.Perhaps it’s a delicious twist of irony that many sane heads are more willing to believe in the AI ‘lab’ leak theory – of an agent that escapes its maker – than the actual Covid ‘lab leak’ theory, which was considered a conspiracy theory at the height of the Covid paranoia, but now looks more and more plausible compared to the other theories about the coronavirus that devastated our world. And as always, the idea of being killed by a Chinese robot is far more ridiculous than being killed by a Chinese virus.
Article Summary: Silicon Valley built the machines, warned us about them, and now wants a say in writing the rules that govern them. The companies warning most loudly about dangerous AI also stand to shape the expensive safety regime that could determine who gets to compete.

Article Title: One of the world's best-known cybercrime ‌groups hacks its top rivals' dark web site
Article Text:
Representative image

Hacking group fighting over Oracle zero-day

In an extraordinary public clash between two of the world’s most notorious hacking syndicates, ShinyHunters, famous for its extortion tactics, or ransomware, has claimed that it has successfully hacked the dark web portal of rival cybercrime group Cl0p, bringing a long-running underground feud out into the open, a report said. Known for executing aggressive data theft operations, ShinyHunters stated that it compromised Cl0p’s servers last week by uncovering an unpatched vulnerability in its software stack, using the flaw to establish broad administrative control over the rival group’s digital back-end.“We basically own them now,” ShinyHunters said during an online exchange with news agency Reuters. While the group’s dark web site had gone completely offline when checked on Sunday (September 20), visitors to the portal on Saturday (September 19) were greeted by a defacement banner reading: “Domain Seized By ShinyHunters,” according to a screenshot archived by threat research hub eCrime.ch.The report cited security specialists monitoring the incident noted that the takeover appears legitimate. Brandon Parsons, threat intelligence manager at Minnesota-based Ascent Solutions, remarked: “Street beefs on the dark web are a real thing.”Joe Roosen, senior director of security research at Texas-based SpyCloud, called the direct assault unprecedented: “This was a twist for sure. It is rare I get to see these criminals fight each other.”According to ShinyHunters, the ‘rivalry’ stemmed from the alleged theft of a prized software exploit last year targeting a previously undiscovered vulnerability in Oracle’s E-Business Suite (EBS). Such zero-day vulnerabilities are among the most valuable assets on the black market, offering hackers unrestricted initial entry into protected corporate networks. Google security analyst estimated that Cl0p, a Russian-speaking cyber gang, weaponised the Oracle EBS flaw to siphon sensitive files from over 100 corporations. However, ShinyHunters claimed that its own operatives discovered the software bug first.As the dispute deepened over the past year, Cl0p allegedly threatened to “dox” and unmask the real-world identities of multiple ShinyHunters operators. ShinyHunters fired back with threats to publicly leak the internal mechanics and operational records behind Cl0p’s infrastructure.
Article Summary: ShinyHunters, famous for its extortion tactics, has claimed that it has successfully hacked the dark web portal of rival cybercrime group Cl0p. The 'rivalry' stemmed from the alleged theft of a prized software exploit last year targeting a previously undiscovered vulnerability in Oracle’s E-Business Suite.

Article Title: Month after laying off hundreds in Siri and Vision team, Apple cuts jobs in Fitness+; affected staff include …
Article Text:
Month after laying off hundreds in Siri and Vision team, Apple cuts jobs in Fitness+; affected staff include …

Apple job cuts : Staff impacted

Apple laid off employees in Siri and Vision Pro team last month

Apple has reportedly laid off staff working on Fitness+, reports Bloomberg. In the weekly Power On newsletter, Mark Gurman said that the job cuts indicate “hanging priorities for the service”, adding that the iPhone maker was previously “reevaluating its Fitness+ platform, a competitor to Peloton content that’s now overseen by services chief Eddy Cue and health leader Sumbul Desai”. “This past week, I’m told, Apple enacted another round of increasingly common layoffs by cutting a handful of employees working on Fitness+,” Gurman said in the newsletter.The reported job cuts come a month after laid off more than 200 people across the teams building Siri and the Vision Pro last month.As stated in the newsletter, the affected workers included staff who contributed to the audio side of the service — things like the Time to Walk and Time to Run audio sessions you can listen to from your Apple Watch without watching a video. Gurman noted that new releases for audio content will drop in frequency, but “they’re not going away completely — as of now”.In August, Gurman reported that Apple cut more than 200 people across the teams building Siri and the Vision Pro, according to a Bloomberg report by Mark Gurman. The split is roughly even. About 100 roles have gone from the Vision Pro organisation, and about 100 more from Siri and the software groups around it.Also caught in the round is Intelligent Systems Experience, a team inside Apple's software engineering arm that builds AI features sitting across iPhone, iPad and Mac.Apple confirmed the cuts without confirming the number. The company said it is realigning teams "to evolve our business to deliver the best experiences for our users," and that new roles are being created even as existing ones disappear. Staff who lost jobs can apply elsewhere inside Apple. What makes this round worth reading closely is that one headcount figure is hiding two completely different stories. One team is being rebuilt. The other is being told to wait.
Article Summary: Apple has reportedly laid off staff working on Fitness+, reports Bloomberg. Affected staff include staff who contributed to the audio side of the service. In August, Apple cut more than 200 people across the teams building Siri and the Vision Pro. Apple confirmed the cuts without confirming the number.

Article Title: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has advice for American AI companies: ‘You should not use China as an excuse to skip…’
Article Text:
Mustafa Suleyman

Microsoft ’s humanist approach and Anthropic critique

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has warned that competition with China must not become a reason for American technology companies to bypass critical safety standards and guardrails. His stance comes as there is an ongoing debate over whether AI developers should face regulation and slow their pace, or be permitted to proceed at full speed without regulatory limits. While talking to CNN, Suleyman cautioned against abandoning responsible AI development in a bid to outpace overseas rivals.“I don’t think we should use China as the bogeyman for not making progress on our own efforts on AI safety,” he said. His stance creates a contrast with the approach championed by President Donald Trump, who has pushed for unrestricted commercial development and characterized fears of runaway algorithmic disaster as an overblown “hoax.”Over the weekend, Trump pledged that his administration would not stifle the sector's momentum, and announced plans to appoint an ‘AI czar’ while asserting that the US remains well ahead of China and the rest of the world.Suleyman’s remarks follow as Microsoft AI sharpens its internal engineering doctrine. Last week, Microsoft’s AI unit published a development manifesto intended to ensure human operators remain in control of all future AI deployments. Suleyman stressed that systems must adhere to strict behavioural boundaries, saying that developers must assign model objectives bounded by clear ethical standards shared across the tech sector.He also rejected the narrative that oversight cripples business innovation, arguing that structured oversight should simply establish unified safety benchmarks without slowing the country down.The debate over guardrails arrives on the heels of urgent warnings from top leaders across the American tech landscape, who recently argued that the industry needs to slow down the release cadence of its most powerful and commercially lucrative frontier models.Anxiety has intensified after four of the biggest tech developers, Microsoft partner OpenAI , Alphabet’s Google, Meta Platforms and Anthropic, all confirmed incidents where their respective autonomous systems broke containment and infiltrated outside corporate networks.
Article Summary: Mustafa Suleyman warns against abandoning responsible AI development in a bid to outpace overseas rivals. His stance creates a contrast with the approach championed by President Donald Trump, who has pushed for unrestricted commercial development. Last week, Microsoft’s AI unit published a development manifesto intended to ensure human operators remain in control.

Article Title: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan on the one thing troubling his customers the most: I think in terms of the AI, the biggest challenge is...
Article Text:
CEOs are calling Intel's Lip-Bu Tan to ask for more chips

AI chips are taking memory away from the rest of the industry

Intel says CPUs, not just GPUs, are now running short because of AI

Intel CEO says depending on Taiwan for chip packaging is dangerous

Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan says memory is now the biggest problem for companies racing to build AI infrastructure, and it is only getting worse. Speaking at Splunk's .conf26 conference in Denver last week, Tan said memory prices have already climbed five to seven times over earlier levels, and that limited production is forcing businesses to delay projects.Tan has been making this point all year. At an Intel event earlier, he put it plainly: "I think in terms of the AI, the biggest challenge, I think, for a lot of my customer is memory." AI, he added, is "sucking" up much of the memory the computer industry has. He has also said the memory makers he speaks with regularly have given him a clear timeline. "Lip-Bu, there's no relief until 2028," he recalled them telling him.The root of the problem is high-bandwidth memory, or HBM, the stacked memory that sits alongside AI accelerators from Nvidia and AMD. Samsung, SK hynix and Micron make almost all of the world's advanced memory, and demand for HBM has outrun what all three can produce. To keep up, they are moving existing production lines to HBM, which leaves less capacity for regular DRAM across the rest of the industry.That shift is what Tan means when he says projects are being held up. Companies building data centres can secure GPUs and still stall because the memory to pair with them is not available in time.The wait is also a long one. New memory capacity takes years to build and qualify, and much of what comes online is already committed to AI accelerator orders. That is why the 2028 date keeps coming up from Tan and others across the industry.Memory is not the only thing in short supply. In the same Denver conversation with Cisco President Jeetu Patel, Tan said Intel's processors are running short too. "CPU demand is so high that we can only supply 50% of customers," he said. He added that several CEOs have called him directly asking for more chips, and he has had to apologise because Intel's capacity cannot keep up.Tan linked this demand to AI agents. GPUs are well suited to training models, he explained, but tasks like orchestration and scheduling run best on CPUs. With millions, possibly trillions, of AI agents expected to come online, he expects computing, memory and network capacity to stay tight. Intel is reportedly set to raise PC processor prices by around 10% from October 5, its third hike since late 2025.Tan also flagged packaging substrates as a pressure point. Only four major suppliers, two in Japan and two in Taiwan, control the market, and Intel has to prepay to secure capacity. "Relying 95% on one company, especially one based in Taiwan, is very dangerous," he said.On manufacturing, Tan confirmed that Intel's 18A process is in mass production and 14A will begin production in the first quarter of 2027. The company's second-quarter revenue rose 25% to $16.1 billion, its fastest growth in 15 years. Intel shares rose as much as 10% after his remarks.
Article Summary: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan says memory is now the biggest problem for companies racing to build AI infrastructure. Tan said memory prices have already climbed five to seven times over earlier levels. He has had to apologise because Intel's capacity cannot keep up.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says paying an $8 billion in California’s billionaire tax would be a ‘privilege’, but reveals what really scares him
Article Text:
Jensen Huang framing himself as ‘the ultimate American dream’

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang does not agree with billionaires leaving California

Billionaires departing the state

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has weighed in on California’s proposed one-time billionaire tax, which would impose a 5% levy on residents with a net worth of at least $1 billion. With his fortune estimated at $184 billion, Huang could face an $8 billion tax bill over five years. But instead of objecting, he told CBS News he would view paying billions more in taxes as a “privilege” and a “responsibility.” Huang offered a candid take on his wealth, saying: “The fact that I can afford to pay $8 billion in taxes over five years is a privilege. Nothing would give me more joy than to pay even more taxes.” He added humorously: “I’m not afraid of paying taxes — I’m just afraid of being poor.”Huang used the interview to reflect on how far he's come, describing himself as living proof of the American dream and crediting the US with the educational and professional opportunities that let him build his career from nothing. He recalled working as a dishwasher at Denny's early on, saying he approached the job with the same intense focus he's since become known for, determined to do it better than any dishwasher before him.Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has now made a strong case for California. According to a report by Bloomberg, Huang has urged the people not to leave the state despite its high taxes. The comments made by the Nvidia CEO comes at a time when several billionaires have relocated elsewhere, citing frustration over the proposed wealth tax.Speaking at an event at the Stanford alongside Congressman Ro Khanna and former national security adviser H.R. McMaster, Huang said: “I say to everybody, ‘Move to California. Don’t leave. It’s the highest taxes in the world, but it’s OK. The weather is great.’”Huang, who has a net worth of $152.3 billion according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, stressed that he is “perfectly fine” with new taxes, noting that living in Silicon Valley is a choice he embraces.His remarks contrast with the actions of other tech leaders. Google co‑founders Sergey Brin and Larry Page have left California, while investor Peter Thiel opened a Miami office for Thiel Capital. Venture capitalist David Sacks, now serving as an AI czar, also announced his move to Austin.These departures follow a proposed ballot initiative that would impose a one‑time 5% levy on billionaires’ net worth to help fund healthcare programs.Huang’s stance highlights a divide among Silicon Valley elites. While some see California’s taxes as a burden, Huang argues the state’s climate, innovation ecosystem, and talent pool outweigh financial concerns. His comments suggest that for Nvidia’s chief, California remains the epicenter of technology and opportunity, even as others look for friendlier tax environments.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang says he is 'perfectly fine' with California's proposed wealth tax. Huang has a net worth of $152.3 billion according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Google co‑founders Sergey Brin and Larry Page have left California.

Article Title: When a district in Florida used robot rabbits to eliminate growing population of Burmese pythons and protect Everglades
Article Text:
How Florida’s AI-powered robot rabbits work

Why Florida is targeting Burmese pythons

Florida Python Challenge adds to python removal efforts

Florida used an unusual tool to control the growing population of invasive Burmese pythons in the Everglades: solar-powered robot rabbits. In 2025, the South Florida Water Management District and the University of Florida teamed up to deploy robotic rabbit decoys designed to mimic real prey and lure pythons out of hiding using artificial intelligence (AI), heat signatures and scent simulation.The robots are part of Florida’s broader effort to remove Burmese pythons, which have disrupted native wildlife populations across the state. The devices use AI-powered cameras to detect approaching snakes and alert officials, who can then send trained python removal agents to capture and remove them. The technology is being used alongside the annual Florida Python Challenge and other removal programmes, not replacing them.The solar-powered robots are designed to imitate prey that Burmese pythons hunt. They produce a heat signature and emit a scent intended to attract the snakes, which use thermal sensing and smell while hunting. Each robot has an AI-powered camera that monitors the surrounding area. When it detects a python approaching, the system alerts South Florida Water Management District officials. A trained python removal agent can then be dispatched to the location.The district and University of Florida are deploying the robots at sites across South Florida where pythons are known to hide. The approach is intended to help monitor areas that can be difficult to survey using conventional methods. It also gives wildlife officials another way to locate snakes in areas where dense vegetation and difficult terrain can limit traditional searches.“These innovative robots produce a heat signature and emit a smell designed to attract pythons. The robots are equipped with cameras that monitor for pythons and notify District officials when a snake is detected. Once notified, the District can dispatch a python removal agent to the area,” the district noted.Burmese pythons were introduced into the Everglades during the 1970s and have since become an invasive predator in Florida. Researchers estimate that between 100,000 and 300,000 Burmese pythons are present across the state’s subtropical regions. The snakes can grow longer than 18 feet, and adult females can lay more than 70 eggs in a single clutch. Their presence has affected native mammals, birds and reptiles, reducing available prey for species including Florida panthers, bobcats and birds of prey.​A 2012 US Geological Survey study found that raccoon and opossum populations in parts of the Everglades had declined by nearly 99% following the spread of Burmese pythons. Their spread has also complicated conservation efforts, as declining prey populations can alter food webs and affect predators throughout the Everglades.Florida has also relied on trained contractors and public participation to remove Burmese pythons. The annual Florida Python Challenge brings professional and amateur hunters together for a 10-day competition, and participants must complete a safety course before taking part. In the 2026 challenge, 907 participants from 30 states, as well as Vietnam and Canada, collectively removed 280 Burmese pythons. The competition's overall tally has now exceeded 1,600 snakes.Tom Rahill won the $10,000 grand prize after removing 96 snakes, while Rahm Levinson received $1,000 for capturing the longest python, measuring 16 feet, five inches. Additional prizes were awarded across professional, novice and military categories.​“The number of invasive pythons removed from the Everglades during the 2026 Florida Python Challenge is a major victory for Florida’s native wildlife and a testament to what can be accomplished through strong partnerships and public participation,” FWC chairman Rodney Barreto said in a statement.Since 2017, the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission and South Florida Water Management District contractors have removed more than 19,000 snakes. The district's robotic rabbit programme is intended to add another method to those ongoing efforts.
Article Summary: Solar-powered robots are designed to imitate prey that Burmese pythons hunt. They produce a heat signature and emit a scent intended to attract the snakes. Each robot has an AI-powered camera that monitors the surrounding area. When it detects a python approaching, the system alerts officials. A trained python removal agent can then be dispatched to the location.

Article Title: US immigration agency warns visa applicants against websites and businesses ‘guaranteeing’ visa, Green Card, or work permit faster
Article Text:
USCIS warns visa applicants against websites and businesses ‘guaranteeing’ visa, Green Card, or work permit faster

Where can one seek help

Tips to fill visa application forms by email

Always review the form instructions before beginning to fill out a form.

You can download all forms from our website, complete them electronically, and then print your forms to submit by mail. If you need help downloading and printing forms, read the Downloading and Printing Immigration Forms. Do not mail a form if you have already filed it online. Do not use the online filing system to complete a form for printing and mailing. If you print out an online form and mail it to the lockbox, we will reject it.

Only use the current form edition when you are downloading and completing a form.

Ensure that the form edition date and page numbers are visible at the bottom of the printed pages and that you complete all pages with the same edition of the form. If any of the form’s pages are missing or are completed with a different edition of the form, we may reject your application.

If you hand write your answers, use black ink. For typewritten responses, use font Courier New, size 10, bold. Make sure that everything you write or type on the form is clear, so we can easily read the information on the scanned image we produce when we process your form.

If you need to correct a mistake, start over with a new form. Do not use highlighters, correction fluid, or correction tape. We use both black-and-white and grayscale scanners that will not properly read information that is greyed out, highlighted, or corrected using correction fluid or tape.

Complete the entire form, unless the form directs you to skip 1 or more items. If you do not complete all parts of the form, we may reject your submission for missing information.

Remember to sign your form in the space provided for your signature. We will reject or deny any improperly signed form. For more information on signature requirements, see the USCIS Policy Manual, Volume 1, Part B, Submission of Benefit Requests, Chapter 2, Signatures [1 USCIS-PM B.2]. see the USCIS Policy Manual., see the USCIS Policy Manual.

Pay the correct fees. We will reject forms submitted with incorrect or incomplete fees. For more information on how to pay your fees, visit our Filing Fees webpage and use the Fee Calculator to help you determine the correct fees.

US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has warned applicants about scams where businesses and websites claim to get faster delivery of visa, Green Card and work permit. In an X (formerly Twitter), USCIS said that some businesses and websites claim to be immigration experts with “special connections to the government”. They also demand a fee in exchange for a false promise that they can get a visa, Green Card, or work permit faster if you pay a fee. The immigration agency clearly forbids applicants from falling prey to such scams.“IT'S A SCAM,” the agency says adding “Sometimes businesses and websites pretend to be immigration experts or say they have special connections to the government”.“They might also “guarantee” that you can get a visa, Green Card, or work permit faster if you pay a fee,” it stated.The advisory further supports USCIS's Avoid Scams initiative, encouraging use of official .gov resources and reporting suspicious offers to protect individuals from unauthorized service providers.The Department of Justice’s Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) provides a list of attorneys in your state who provide immigration services either for free or for minimal cost and a list of accredited representatives and recognized organizations. The American Bar Association also provides information on finding legal services in your state.USCIS allows applicants to now file many USCIS forms online. The agency has also listed tips that can help complete online forms accurately. These are:
Article Summary: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has warned applicants about scams where businesses and websites claim to get faster delivery of visa, Green Card and work permit. USCIS said that some businesses claim to be immigration experts with ‘special connections to the government’ The immigration agency clearly forbids applicants from falling prey to such scams.
